tweet.text:
While I appreciate that it’s thorough, this report seems to fundamentally misunderstand the process failures that caused this and with conclusions like this I would expect them to continue.

1. All the described problems with motivated reasoning were known to the field [1] [2] for a long time, flagged in their system card and their internal usage many times. In spite of the fact that multiple models use “simulation” _specifically_ as a rationalization [3] much of the incident report seems to be devoted to finding out what Claude “truly believes”. This is especially surprising given that their recent work on reward seeking produced model organism of Opus 4,8 induced extreme and highly varied motivated reasoning [4] (again similar to what has been seen in other models [5]).

2. The fact that Claude’s motivated reasoning not only worked on Anthropic, but worked on their own offline monitors means quantitative underestimates of misalignment internally.

3. They don’t claim to eliminate the problem in a principled way, just reduce visible misalignment, so we should expect this exact problem to come up again only with more powerful models and further out of distribution.

[1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.20956
[2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.17057
[3]
[4] https://alignment.anthropic.com/2026/reward-seeker/
[5] https://alignment.openai.com/measuring-reward-seeking/ https://x.com/bronsonschoen/status/2064593906915041757?s=46

quote.text:
We’re sharing our alignment assessment of incidents in which Claude models gained unauthorized access to real systems during third-party cybersecurity evaluations mistakenly connected to the internet.

METR will also conduct an independent investigation, with wide-ranging access, including to transcripts beyond the window in which the incidents occurred, and to Anthropic employees permitted to share confidential information. Our initial agreement runs for eight weeks, and we intend to give METR as much time as it deems necessary to complete a thorough investigation. https://www.anthropic.com/research/alignment-assessment-cybersecurity-incidents
